title: Was the Bills’ defense a concern? Josh Allen delivers vs. Texans, but Buffalo’s new-look unit struggles
content:
HOUSTON — Josh Allen connected with Joshua Palmer for the go-ahead 34-yard touchdown late in the fourth quarter as the Buffalo Bills ended their woes in Houston with a 36-31 win over the Texans.

It’s Allen’s first career win as a starter against the Texans in Houston (he was previously 0-4). It’s the Bills’ first win in Houston since 2006.

Allen threw for 334 yards and two touchdowns on 20-of-29 passing. He also ran for a pair of scores. Offseason trade acquisition DJ Moore caught five passes for 100 yards and a touchdown in his debut. Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid, coming off last season’s torn PCL, was a major target for Allen, too, with five catches for 130 yards.

The 36 points are the most the Texans defense has given up since December 2023.

The Texans were threatening late on a potential game-winning drive, but a Deone Walker sack and Greg Rousseau’s forced fumble sealed the win for the Bills.

The Bills have a short week, as they officially open the new Highmark Stadium against the Detroit Lions on Thursday night. The Texans host the Cincinnati Bengals next Sunday.

Box score | Week 1 live blog | Game discussion

The projections of both teams being near the top of the list seem dead on, as both teams showed a high ceiling. For the Bills and their new-look deep-passing attack with wide receiver DJ Moore, their ability to get chunk plays against a fantastic Texans defense really stands out. It should give the Bills confidence they can move the ball against most of the league’s better defenses if they’re on their game.

For the Texans, their offense looked much improved from a year ago and helped spoil Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard’s debut with four touchdowns. While both the Bills and Texans will hope for better results from their defense, both teams appear to be right in the race for the AFC this season. — Joe Buscaglia, staff writer

Holistically, the Bills didn’t look much different Sunday than they did under Sean McDermott, but they enjoyed much more success against an opponent that annihilated them last year.

The offense put up a ton of points, but the defense looked more bend-but-don’t-break than like the aggressive unit everyone expected from new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard, a star pupil from the Rex Ryan/Mike Pettine school.

The Texans sacked Allen eight times last year and generated a bunch of takeaways, but the 2024 MVP was clean in both regards and delivered late-game heroics we’ve come to expect. Allen ran for a pair of touchdowns and threw for two more, including the 34-yard winner to Joshua Palmer with 1:36 to play. Running back James Cook looked like a potential gamebreaker when given the opportunity. Moore provided a jolt but limped off the field late in the fourth quarter.

But first impressions of the defense — the side of the ball the Bills wanted to improve when they fired McDermott — left much to be desired. Chunk plays and bad penalties plagued Leonhard’s crew all afternoon. The secondary endured a grueling game in both categories, but forcing a couple of C.J. Stroud fumbles — the last one with nine seconds left — saved the day. — Tim Graham, senior writer

We learned that they are packaging their personnel differently than last year, but the Bills definitely looked like a team with a lot of new defensive starters in a brand-new scheme. There were some highlights, with the Bills forcing strip-sacks both to begin the game and to end it, and then getting off the field in a three-and-out when the Texans were trying to run out the clock. However, between those events, the Texans made big gains, the Bills failed to stop third down, and Leonhard’s unit has a lot to improve.

All three levels of the field raised questions. The pass rush wasn’t consistent enough, the run defense struggled to get off blocks, and there were some big gains through the air, too. A shootout against this Texans team was a bit unexpected, but it might mean the Bills need to be a shootout team early in the season and rely on Allen and the offense. Still, there were some signs of life for Leonhard’s defense, despite surrendering 31 points. — Buscaglia

You could tell by the smile on Allen’s face that he marveled at Moore’s flair for the dramatic. Allen and Brady didn’t target Moore until less than five minutes remained before halftime. Yet over the next seven snaps Moore accounted for 122 yards in just 90 seconds, and the Bills scored two touchdowns.

Their initial connection went for 18 yards and was followed by an end-zone strike that resulted in a 46-yard pass interference call on cornerback Kamari Lassiter. Allen ran the final yard for the score.

On the second snap of the next possession, Allen hit Moore for 15 yards and on the next play fired a strike up the right sideline. Texans safety Reed Blankenship nearly got his hands on it, but Moore made the catch and – with nobody behind him – cruised for a 43-yard TD. Allen beamed as he raised his arms and watched Moore finish the play.

What a debut it was. Buffalo has been looking for a reliable, field-stretching wideout since trading Stefon Diggs in 2024. Bills fans have been excited about Moore’s potential production even if futures betting pegged him for lower-key stats (65.5 receptions for 800.5 yards and 5.5 TDs), he has gotten off to the kind of start that should keep folks excited.

Moore finished with five catches for 100 yards, but Allen didn’t connect with him for most of the third quarter and all of the fourth. — Graham

Could it be both? While the Texans have had Allen’s number in Houston, it’s foolish to think the 2024 MVP wouldn’t break through eventually. The Texans only sacked Allen twice and Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter’s names weren’t called very much. Moore and Kincaid were a handful and costly penalties on Lassiter and the Texans’ secondary were too much to overcome.

Last year, the Texans’ defense kept Houston in games all season. Today, Stroud and the offense led the way. It’s only Week 1, but that was a far cry from the Texans’ defense we’ve been used to seeing and that won’t cut it against the top AFC teams. — Adam Coleman, NFL editor
